thread:
customer_joe: Hey team, after we put the L7 terminator in front of our app the SSE streams from Redwood are frequently truncating mid-event. Client sees a partial JSON blob and then a reconnect. Happens with both h2 and h1 clients.

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Joe. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl or client) and any proxy config you added? Also any request IDs from the server side would help.

customer_joe: Repro is simple: we post a long chat completion request and subscribe to server-sent events. Through the terminator it often drops in the middle of a chunk. Curl repro:```bash
curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"gpt-x","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long prompt"}]}'
```
We see repeated 204/206-like behavior but not full stream. No errors in our app logs.

kevin_sre: Can you share the L7 terminator vendor and config snippet? Hoping to see if it's doing midstream buffer flush or connection pooling to a backend that speaks h1.

customer_joe: It's an internal L4/L7 appliance (proprietary) that terminates TLS and forwards to our backend on HTTP/1.1 keep-alive. Config excerpt:```text
upstream: backend_pool
keepalive: true
max_chunk_buffer: 16kb
idle_timeout: 30s
http_version: 1.1
strip_te: true
```
We tried increasing buffer but still see partial events.

maria_support: Two quick hypotheses: 1) Terminator coalesces or splits chunk boundaries when translating h2->h1 causing SSE event framing to break; 2) It prematurely sends a 0-length chunk or connection pool reuse that yields a perceived EOF to clients. Can you capture a raw tcp dump across the terminator to see chunk boundaries?

customer_joe: We captured pcap. I can share a small hex diff but here's the key: after ~12s the terminator sends a CRLF and then immediately reuses the backend connection for a different request, clients (esp browsers) interpret that as stream end and reconnect.

ops-bot: Billing alert: spike detected for org acme-corp — 18x connection attempts over 12m — possible reconnect storm. ticket: BILL-4592

billing-bot: @maria_support flagged — customer reported unexpected cost from reconnects. Recommend temporary rate-limiter or retry-backoff on our side while root cause investigated.

kevin_sre: Thanks — looks like the terminator's HTTP/1.1 translator is not honoring chunked streaming semantics when connection: keep-alive plus connection pooling are enabled. Quick test I ran (from our side) against a toy terminator shows boundary merging that produces mid-event packetization. Repro command I used:```bash
echo -e "GET /stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nAccept: text/event-stream\r\n\r\n" | nc localhost 8080 | sed -n '1,120p'
```
Results show repeated 0-length chunk markers followed by unrelated headers.

julia_eng: Assigning eng-runtime to look at server side: @kevin_sre can you capture the request-id headers (x-rw-request-id) that make it to our edge? Also we should test forcing `TE: trailers` and ensure the terminator does not strip TE. On our side we can add a temporary edge-side reconnect coalescing (client-visible event id) but that's a bandaid.

customer_joe: x-rw-request-id: rw-20241103-0a1b2c3d (from one truncated run). We can share more pcaps privately. Workaround for us: disabling keep-alive on terminator resolved it but not acceptable at scale.

maria_support: Steps we'll take: 1) escalate to eng-platform (julia) to validate TE/trailers/pass-through behavior; 2) suggest customer set terminator to preserve Transfer-Encoding: chunked and disable downstream request multiplexing; 3) provide a server-side mitigation patch to add explicit SSE keepalive comments (":" lines) and event-id fencing to reduce client reconnection load.

julia_eng: Putting a short-term runbook: - If you control terminator, set http_version: 2.0 passthrough or enable chunked passthrough; if not, place a TCP passthrough for the /v1/stream path. - Add SSE ping comments from the app every 5s to prevent idle timeouts. - We'll open ENG-STREAM-857 to design a durable solution (edge preserves chunk boundaries on h2->h1 translations).

kevin_sre: Filed ENG-STREAM-857 and linked pcap in the ticket. Also noted we should add a synthetic integration test in proxy testsuite that simulates h2->h1 translator merging chunks.

customer_joe: Appreciate the quick triage. For immediate relief we enabled longer keepalive and disabled request pooling for stream endpoints, which reduced reconnects by ~90%. We'll await ENG-STREAM-857. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Thanks Joe — keeping this open until ENG confirms deploy. If billing team needs to credit for spike, please open BILL-4592 followup and we'll coordinate.
